ropeway:dlg-guide-body: A tower is 16 blocks: the pylon footing you already placed, plus 15 more. One crossarm on two legs - it is a doorway, not a tunnel. 1. Two posts of four blocks each, standing on the ground three blocks either side of the footing - logs, debarked logs, planks, raw stone, cobblestone, drystone, polished rock or stone bricks, whichever suits what you build in. 2. A seven-wide crossarm across their tops: the pylon head in the middle, directly four above the footing, and three ropeway braces either side of it. That leaves a clear 5 wide, 4 tall archway, and the cabin passes through it along the axis the footing's block info panel names - so face the footing down the line before you build. That axis is the heading the cabin holds the whole time it is in the frame; it turns for the next span only once it is clear of the posts. Right-click the footing to light up every cell that is still wrong: red where the wrong block sits, the wanted block's own colour where nothing does. Riding: sit down and the cabin runs to the end of the line. Press {0} to get off at a tower in between - each press steps the selection one tower further along, and past the end of the line it comes back the other way. Press {1} for an outside view of the cabin while you ride, and again to come back inside. Both are listed in Settings > Controls if you would rather move them. Freight: Ctrl and right-click a bench holding a basket or a chest to load it onto that bench. Right-click a loaded bench to open it. A loaded bench cannot be sat on, so a cabin carries two loads, or one load and one passenger. Ctrl and right-click a bench with an empty hand to take the container off again - it has to be emptied first.
